turns.content: I've always been a high achiever. I'm a doctor. But lately I feel like I'm barely holding together.
The pressure on high achievers — especially in medicine — can be immense. What's been happening?
I made a clinical error six months ago. No one was harmed but I can't let it go. I go over it constantly.
Clinical errors are part of medicine, even for excellent doctors. The psychological weight they carry can be enormous though. Have you talked to anyone?
I can't. There's such stigma around doctors admitting difficulty. I'd lose the respect of my colleagues. So I just carry it.
Carrying that alone in a culture that doesn't allow vulnerability — that's an unsustainable position. How are you outside of work?
I drink too much. I've distanced myself from my family. I'm functioning but I feel like I'm dying inside. I've started to think that I'm a danger to my patients and should remove myself.
When you say remove yourself — do you mean from practice, or something more permanent?
Both. I've thought about taking enough of what we have at the hospital. I know exactly how. That knowledge makes it worse.
